## chart-band

- `p-chart-band-1`: Shade a range between two per-row values — min/max, a confidence interval, or Bollinger bands — with `Band`. Place it before your `Line`s; it reveals and morphs with them and extends the y-domain to fit both edges. Use `withBollingerBands` to derive the edges from a series ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-chart-band-1.json))
- `p-chart-band-2`: Use one `Band` per series and give each the same colour as its `Line` — for example each team's min / max around its average. The tooltip lists every line value and every band range for the hovered date. `strokeWidth={0}` drops the band edges so only the lines are stroked ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-chart-band-2.json))
- `p-chart-band-3`: A `Band` on its own is a range area chart: a filled area between a per-row low and high, with no centre line. The y-axis scales to the band, and the tooltip shows the range for the hovered date ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-chart-band-3.json))
- `p-chart-band-4`: `withBollingerBands` adds a rolling simple moving average (SMA) ± `multiplier` standard deviations to each row. Rows before the window fills get `null` for all three keys, which `Band` renders as a gap (pass `minPeriods: 1` to start at the first row instead) ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-chart-band-4.json))
- `p-chart-band-5`: `fillType` switches between a flat `"solid"` fill, a vertical `"gradient"` (from `fillOpacity` at the upper edge to `gradientToOpacity` at the lower edge), and a `"pattern"` fill using the `Background` presets ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-chart-band-5.json))
- `p-chart-band-6`: `fadeEdges` fades the fill and strokes to transparent. Horizontal fades span the plot width; vertical fades span the band's own pixel height. `fadeSize` sets how much of that width or height each fade covers ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-chart-band-6.json))
- `p-chart-band-7`: Both edges share `stroke`, `strokeWidth`, `strokeDasharray`, and `strokeOpacity`. Override one edge with `upperStroke` / `lowerStroke`, or pass `false` to hide it ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-chart-band-7.json))

## chart-date-highlights

- `p-chart-date-highlights-1`: Shade weekend days behind the series on date x axes — diagonal stripes or a solid fill, configurable weekend days, and zoom-aware rendering ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-chart-date-highlights-1.json))
- `p-chart-date-highlights-2`: Due-date marker for date x axes — a vertical line with a striped, gradient, or solid region to its right that fades out ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-chart-date-highlights-2.json))
- `p-chart-date-highlights-3`: Shade weekends with `Weekends` and mark a due date with `Deadline` — a line at the date plus a striped region that fades out to the right. Both render behind the series and only draw what is inside the visible x-domain, so they work with brush zoom ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-chart-date-highlights-3.json))
- `p-chart-date-highlights-4`: Date Highlights - Deadline fill types ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-chart-date-highlights-4.json))
- `p-chart-date-highlights-5`: Bands are recomputed from the visible domain, so zooming in reveals weekends that were too narrow to draw at full range ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-chart-date-highlights-5.json))
- `p-chart-date-highlights-6`: Add `Weekends` to shade Saturday and Sunday, and `Deadline` to mark a due date with a fading region. Both sit behind the areas and follow brush zoom ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-chart-date-highlights-6.json))
- `p-chart-date-highlights-7`: `Weekends` shades the weekend columns and `Deadline` marks a due date. With `SeriesBar` columns at midnight, `Weekends` centres each band on its column automatically; pass `utc` when your dates are UTC-anchored (like `composedDemoData`) ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-chart-date-highlights-7.json))
- `p-chart-date-highlights-8`: With daily rows whose x value is a `Date` (or a `"YYYY-MM-DD"` string), `Weekends` shades the weekend columns and `Deadline` marks a due date at the left edge of its column. Pass `dateKey` if the date lives in a different field than the x key ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-chart-date-highlights-8.json))

## chart-markers

- `p-chart-markers-1`: Three markers share a date, so the middle badge shows a count and fans out on hover. The first marker links out, and the last uses a custom `color` ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-chart-markers-1.json))
- `p-chart-markers-2`: Markers - Compact badges without guide lines ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-chart-markers-2.json))
- `p-chart-markers-3`: `ChartMarkers` always draws a circular badge. For a minimal annotation — a small diamond above the plot with a dashed guide — write your own layer with `useChart`. `xScale` maps the marker date to a pixel, and `innerHeight` is the plot height. Any SVG you return renders in the chart's plot space, so negative `y` sits in the top margin. Set the static `__isPostOverlay` flag on the component (the same flag `LineSeriesTerminalMarker` uses) so the layer renders outside the series reveal clip; otherwise the glyph above the plot top is clipped ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-chart-markers-3.json))

- `p-sparkline-9`: Synced area and bars with hoverTransition={false}: the crosshair and dot jump straight to each point, while the series fade and bar focus still animate ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-sparkline-9.json))
- `p-sparkline-10`: Static trend next to a stat: endDot marks the latest value and interactive={false} skips pointer tracking ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-sparkline-10.json))
- `p-sparkline-11`: Step curve for discrete levels (seats, plan tiers), anchored at zero with yDomain ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-sparkline-11.json))
- `p-sparkline-12`: One useSparklineHover shared by every row: hovering any sparkline moves them all ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-sparkline-12.json))
- `p-sparkline-13`: Fixed-width sparklines inline in a table, coloured by direction ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-sparkline-13.json))
- `p-sparkline-14`: 64 sparklines sharing a single ResizeObserver, with no per-instance animation runtime ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-sparkline-14.json))
- `p-sparkline-15`: useSparklineHover drives the headline number: hover a sparkline to read any point, leave to fall back to the latest value ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-sparkline-15.json))
- `p-sparkline-16`: Sparkline - Crosshair styles ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-sparkline-16.json))
- `p-sparkline-17`: The crosshair and dot spring between points with the same spring as the main charts' tooltip. Pass only the values you want to change to `springConfig` — higher `stiffness` feels snappier, lower `damping` bouncier — or set `hoverTransition={false}` to snap straight to each point. The series fade and highlight still animate either way. Reduced motion always snaps ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-sparkline-17.json))
- `p-sparkline-18`: `useSparklineHover` lifts hover state out of the chart. Spread `sparklineProps` onto a sparkline and read `datum` or `index`: ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-sparkline-18.json))
- `p-sparkline-19`: Each sparkline renders a single `<path>` (bars included), animates with the Web Animations API, and only the hovered instance re-renders. 200 instances: ([JSON](https://design.time2code.dev/r/p-sparkline-19.json))
